segments: 216. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Amir Tuqaq died,
and the Khaqan took Seljuq,
and he was brought up in the palace, and he loved him greatly.
And one day, when he went in to the Khaqan as was his custom,
the queen observed him closely and gestured to the king:
"Since he is still a boy,
and has all this boldness toward us,
when he grows up, what will he be like?" But when Amir Seljuq sensed this,
he left and took the sons of his clan with him secretly.
And they set out with a great number of horses, herds of camels, sheep, and cattle,
and departed from the land of Turan,
that is to say, of the Turks,
to the land of Iran,
that is to say, of the Persians,
in the manner of shepherds.
And when they saw that Persia was well provided with prosperity,
they took counsel together and said:
"If we do not enter the religion of the inhabitants of the country toward which we are inclined and headed,
no one will join with us,
and we shall be diminished and captured."
And they all agreed,
and sent to the city of Zandah in the territory of Khwarazm,
which was near the desert in which they were pasturing.
And they requested a scribe from the governor there,
to teach them how to worship God.
And he, with great joy, sent them a certain old scribe with gifts and presents,
and he instructed them.
And they remained there for years,
and grew prosperous and multiplied greatly.
And four sons were born to Amir Seljuq:
Michael,
and Yabghu (Payghu {OCR?}),
and Musa,
and Arslan.
And to Michael again were born two sons:
Muhammad, who is Tughril Beg,
and David, who is Chaghri Beg.
And this Chaghri Beg gathered a large force of Turkmens,
and went and plundered places in Armenia and Khorasan.
And he returned to Tughril Beg, his brother, and said to him:
"Here there are two great rulers:
Khwarazmshah Harun,
and Sultan Mas'ud son of Mahmud son of Sebuktegin;
and we are not able to contend with them.
Rather, let us cross into Khorasan and Armenia, which I have scouted,
for I saw no one in them who would stand against us."
And his brother was persuaded by his counsel,
and they arose and crossed the Jayhun, the river of Persia.
And they came upon the city of Damghan,
and destroyed it completely.
And from there they came to the city of Semnan,
and conquered it as well.
